conventions.convention: Finite-array norms use counting sums; the counting inner product is linear in its first argument. All three norms and the inner product are zero on an empty index set.

Type 1 uses exp(-2πi k·x), type 2 uses exp(+2πi k·x), and the mode box includes both endpoints -K_r and K_r. Type-1/type-2 coordinates are period-one representatives; type 3 uses real frequencies and has no implicit wrapping or scaling.
The periodized kernel is φ_τ(x)=Σ_n exp(-π(x+n)²/τ), with τ>0 and period one.
The Gaussian Fourier-series statement assumes Countable Choice and uses the multiplier √τ exp(-πτr²).
The grid DFT has normalization 1/P. Signed mode k occupies the least-nonnegative-residue slot κ(k); M_r>2K_r makes those slots distinct.
Spread neighborhoods include the distance endpoint w_r/M_r, and require M_r≥2w_r+1. Image truncation instead retains integer images -L_r through L_r after reducing displacement to [0,1).

Inputs are exact finite dyadics; candidates and refinement controls are finite. Interval arithmetic admits subnormal endpoints, while the selected operationwise FFT model requires successful no-range-failure operations. Every used twiddle certificate must meet the supplied bound, including a literal zero bound.

Certification requires the complete outward absolute-error bound to meet a positive requested tolerance. Exhausting candidates returns inconclusive; the N=0 branch returns exact zero type-1 output or empty type-2 output with zero radii.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For the stated finite source data, positive τ_r and integers M_r>2K_r, the normalized periodized-grid DFT equals Σ_q Φ̂(k+q⊙M)Σ_j c_j exp(-2πi(k+q⊙M)·x_j). After division by Φ̂(k)>0, its error from F_k is at most AΣ_j|c_j|, where s_r=exp(-πτ_rM_r(M_r-2K_r)) and A=∏_r(1+2s_r/(1-s_r))-1.

For d≥1, τ_r>0 and integers M_r,w_r≥1 with M_r≥2w_r+1, the omitted spreading mass outside W(x) is at most T_d=Σ_r T_r∏_{s≠r}S_s, where a_r=π/(τ_rM_r²), S_r=2/(1-exp(-a_r)) and T_r=2exp(-a_rw_r²)(1+1/(2a_rw_r)). Each full one-coordinate grid mass is at most S_r.

On the specified exact dyadic type-1/type-2 data and finite controls, process the finite candidate list in order, using outward Gaussian enclosures, guarded positive deconvolution, checked computed unitary FFTs and complete error certificates. Return the first candidate meeting the requested positive tolerance as certified, or inconclusive with the first recorded non-success reason after exhaustion; malformed controls return invalid-input.

Assume Countable Choice. For τ>0, the Fourier coefficient of φ_τ at each integer r is √τ exp(-πτr²), and φ_τ(x)=Σ_r √τ exp(-πτr²)exp(2πirx). The periodized series converges locally uniformly, and the Fourier series converges absolutely and uniformly.
For τ>0, integer L≥1 and x∈[0,1], the finite image sum φ_{τ,L} retaining -L≤n≤L satisfies 0≤φ_τ(x)-φ_{τ,L}(x)≤2exp(-πL²/τ)/(1-exp(-πL/τ)); the denominator is positive.

Assume Countable Choice and the algorithm's input hypotheses. For a successful candidate, ε_ana≥α+T_d/(Pd_min), and the returned centers satisfy ‖F̂-F‖∞≤ε_ana‖c‖₁+B_round and ‖ĝ-A*f‖∞≤ε_ana‖f‖₁+B_round*. The N=0 errors are zero. For fixed dimension, bounded widths and image cutoffs, and fixed interval-series controls, one candidate has scalar work O(P log P+Nw^d), apart from the stated elementary-range evaluation work; no type-3 cost claim follows.
For a finite index set E and arrays x,y∈ℂ^E, the Euclidean norm of def-nufft-finite-array-norms satisfies ‖x+y‖₂≤‖x‖₂+‖y‖₂.
